newsitem.title: UK: UK's Labour wins key seat of Basildon.
newsitem.headline: UK's Labour wins key seat of Basildon.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party has won the key seat of Basildon, number 29 on its list of most winnable seats.

The 13,280 majority represented a swing to Labour of 15 percent. The seat achieved mythical status at the 1992 election when the Conservatives held on against the odds with a majority of 2,646, giving an early indication the ruling party was heading for a shock win. The constituency contains a large number of skilled manual labourers, many of whom flourished under Conservative rule in the 1980s. It also boasts the highest proportion of readers of The Sun, Britain's most popular tabloid.
The paper backed the Conservatives at the last election, claiming afterwards it had played a pivotal role in returning the Tories to power.
This time The Sun departed from its right-wing roots and backed the Labour Party.
